title: Car Accident FNOL – Standard Operating Procedure
content:
Super Insurance – Car Accident First Notice of Loss (FNOL)

Procedure:
1. Confirm the safety of all parties involved in the accident.
2. Record the date, time, and specific location of the incident.
3. Obtain a brief description of how the accident occurred.
4. Determine whether the vehicle is drivable or requires towing.
5. Advise the caller not to admit fault to any other parties at the scene.
6. If a police report was filed, collect the report number.
7. Inform the caller that a claims adjuster will contact them within 24-48 hours to assess the damage and guide next steps.
8. This procedure covers the initial property damage and liability claim intake.

title: Car Theft FNOL – Reporting Procedures
content:
Super Insurance – Vehicle Theft Reporting

Procedure:
1. A police report is mandatory for all theft claims. If one has not been filed, the caller must file one before the claim can proceed.
2. Collect the police report number and the reporting station.
3. Record the last known location and time the vehicle was last seen.
4. Note whether the vehicle had any tracking devices (GPS, LoJack, etc.).
5. Confirm vehicle details: make, model, year, color, VIN, and license plate.
6. Verify that all keys are accounted for.
7. Theft claims require a 30-day waiting period before settlement can begin.
8. If the vehicle has an outstanding loan or lease, the caller should notify their lender.
9. Claims exceeding ₹20,00,000 are automatically referred to the Special Investigations Unit (SIU) for review.

title: Towing & Rental Coverage Policy
content:
Super Insurance – Towing & Vehicle Replacement Coverage

Coverage Rules:
- Towing and Roadside Assistance is included with Comprehensive policies and the Roadside Assistance add-on.
- Covered towing is authorized up to ₹12,000 per incident.
- Rental vehicle reimbursement is available only with the Rental Reimbursement add-on (₹3,000/day for up to 30 days).
- Third-Party Only liability policies do not include towing, roadside, or rental coverage.
- For uncovered policyholders, towing and rental services can still be arranged but are billed directly to the customer as out-of-pocket expenses.

title: Vehicle Vandalism Claims
content:
Super Insurance – Vandalism Claim Procedure

Procedure:
1. A police report is required for all vandalism claims.
2. Document the type of damage: keyed paint, broken windows, slashed tires, graffiti, etc.
3. Vandalism falls under Comprehensive coverage. The policyholder must hold a Comprehensive policy for the claim to be valid.
4. The standard Comprehensive deductible applies (typically ₹10,000 or ₹25,000).
5. Photographs of the damage are required (minimum 4 angles).
6. An adjuster visit will be scheduled, or the caller may visit an approved repair facility.
7. Filing a vandalism claim generally does not affect the policyholder's premium.

title: Required Documents – Car Insurance Claims
content:
Super Insurance – Car Claims Documentation Checklist

Required Documents:
- Police report (mandatory for theft, vandalism, and hit-and-run claims)
- Photographs of vehicle damage (minimum 4 angles)
- Third-party insurance details and contact information (for multi-vehicle collisions)
- Written repair estimate from an independent or approved facility
- Driving license of the person operating the vehicle at the time of incident

Note: The agent collects preliminary details during the FNOL call. The assigned Claims Adjuster will request formal documentation during the assessment phase.

title: Life Insurance Death Claim – Filing Procedures
content:
Super Insurance – Life Insurance Death Claim Procedure

Procedure:
1. Express condolences to the caller sincerely and professionally.
2. Locate the policy using the policy number or the registered phone number.
3. Verify the caller's full legal name against the beneficiary records on file.
4. Record the following details about the insured's passing:
   - Date of death
   - Location of death
   - Cause of death
5. Required documents for claim processing:
   - Certified death certificate (original or certified copy)
   - Completed beneficiary claim form (to be mailed or emailed to the caller)
   - Government-issued photo ID of the claimant
6. Payout timeline: Claims are typically processed within 30-60 days after all documents are received.
7. Payout options available: lump sum, installments, or annuity.
8. If the death occurred within the 2-year contestability period, the claim is subject to additional review by the Underwriting department.

title: Life Insurance – Accidental Death Benefits (AD&D)
content:
Super Insurance – Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Coverage

Overview:
AD&D pays an additional benefit (typically equal to the base coverage amount) if the insured's death results from a qualifying accident.

Covered Events:
- Motor vehicle accidents
- Falls
- Drowning
- Other sudden, unforeseen accidents

Exclusions:
- Death due to illness or natural causes
- Suicide
- Drug overdose
- Participation in illegal activities

Additional Documents Required:
- Police report or official accident report
- Autopsy report (if performed)
- Medical examiner's findings

Processing: AD&D claims are reviewed by the Special Claims Unit. Processing time is 60-90 days.

title: Life Insurance – Beneficiary Verification Process
content:
Super Insurance – Beneficiary Verification Standards

Verification Steps:
1. The beneficiary's full legal name must match the policy records.
2. Confirm date of birth, Aadhaar/PAN number (last 4 digits), and current address.
3. Minor beneficiaries: A legal guardian or appointed trustee must file the claim.
4. Multiple beneficiaries: Each beneficiary files a separate claim for their designated share.
5. Deceased beneficiary: The contingent (secondary) beneficiary is contacted.
6. No named beneficiary: The payout is directed to the insured's estate.
7. Disputed beneficiaries: The claim is placed on hold and referred to the Legal department.

Privacy: All beneficiary information is protected under HIPAA and must not be disclosed to unauthorized parties.

title: Life Insurance – Required Documentation Checklist
content:
Super Insurance – Life Insurance Claims Document Checklist

Required:
□ Certified death certificate (original or certified copy)
□ Completed beneficiary claim form
□ Government-issued photo ID of the claimant

Conditional:
□ Proof of relationship to the insured (if claimant is not a named beneficiary)
□ Policy document (if available, not mandatory)
□ Medical records or autopsy report (required for AD&D claims or contestability review)
□ Police report (required for accidental death claims)
□ Power of Attorney documents (if filing on behalf of another beneficiary)
□ Court order (for contested or disputed claims)

title: Fraud Indicators – Red Flags Reference Guide
content:
Super Insurance – Fraud Detection Reference

Common Red Flags:
- Claim filed immediately after policy inception or a recent coverage increase
- Caller demonstrates unusual familiarity with the claims process
- Description of events sounds inconsistent or rehearsed
- Incident occurred in a remote location with no witnesses
- Caller is pressuring for an expedited settlement
- Vehicle was recently listed for sale prior to a theft claim
- Comprehensive coverage was recently added before a theft or vandalism claim
- Multiple prior claims filed within a short period

Protocol: If any red flags are observed, document them in the claim notes and flag the file for SIU (Special Investigations Unit) review. Do not confront or accuse the caller.
